input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there
task: research/buildbot-sheathing milestone 37: a held-joint preload against the wrist F/T sensor's backlash floor

errors.what: first smoke run of experiments/m37_preload/run.py ran 20x slow (load 8 on 4 cores) because numpy/scipy BLAS threads oversubscribed inside a 4-process pool; killed it, set OMP/OPENBLAS/MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 at the top of run.py; full run then took 965 s

doc_friction.issue: The OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 warning is framed for 'GP/BLAS experiments'; a plain multiprocessing pool over scipy SLSQP/HiGHS plus numpy pinv hit the same 20x oversubscription. Worth saying 'any multiprocessing pool over numpy/scipy'.
The pkill/pgrep hook also refuses a bracketed pattern if the plain word appears elsewhere in the same command line (e.g. a later 'python3 run.py'); one wasted call.

deviations.why: Section A's census and the hedge results were extended post hoc to all margins (the registered census was m = 0 only); kept and labelled 'post hoc (not registered)' in results.txt rather than dropped, since it is what explains H137's refutation.
deviations.did: printed the post hoc census separately from the registered one
deviations.result: H136 judged only on the registered m = 0 census

notes: Programme drawn by pick_track.py (buildbot-sheathing). Hypotheses H136-H140 registered and pushed (PR opened as draft) before any computation. Result: under a plan-once / settle error model, 92% of mispredicted joints are the balance controller's own held joints pinned at tau_f; a 0.1 N m leg-joint preload removes them and restores milestone 36's figures (G1 0-20 N stack 56.48 -> 1.64 points); the remaining 0.3-0.8 mm floor is waist/arm joints. H136, H139 held; H137, H138, H140 refuted.
